title: Ireland's Public-Sector Strike Exposes the Fault Lines Beneath a Prosperous… · 26 Oct
keywords: Ireland, public sector strike, pay dispute, corporation tax, fiscal risk, multinationals, unions, Budget 2027, Workplace Relations Commission, public services, inflation, European economy
notes: More than 300,000 Irish public-sector workers walked off the job in a dispute that goes beyond wages, raising fundamental questions about how the state distributes its wealth. Ireland's headline budget surpluses mask a growing dependence on corporation-tax receipts from a handful of multinationals, making the government's room for manoeuvre less certain than it appears. The standoff between unions and ministers has opened a wider debate about whether Ireland's prosperity is built on durable foundations.
